chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mu‘awiyah, from ‘Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ibrahim ibn Khalaf ibn ‘Abbad al-Anmati, from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu ‘Abdillah (عليه السلام), and with him in the house were some people. So I thought that by this he only intended someone other than me. Then he said: “Indeed, by Allah, the Master of this أمر will surely be absent from you, and this matter will surely become obscure until it is said: ‘He died, he perished, in which valley did he go?’ And you will surely be overturned just as a ship is overturned in the waves of the sea. None will be saved except one whose covenant Allah has taken, and in whose heart He has written iman, and whom He has strengthened with a spirit from Him. And twelve ambiguous banners will surely be raised, such that it will not be known which is which.”

He said: So I wept. He said: “What makes you weep, O Abu ‘Abdillah?” I said: “May I be made your ransom, how should I not weep while you are saying: twelve ambiguous banners will be raised, and it will not be known which is which?”
He said: And in his gathering there was an opening through which the sun entered. So he said: “Is this clear?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Our matter is clearer than this sun.”

key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: our matter, i.e. the affair and truth of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: faith firmly inscribed in the heart
key_terms.رَايَةً مُشْتَبِهَةً: an ambiguous banner or confusing claim to allegiance/leadership
key_terms.رُوحٍ مِنْهُ: a spirit from Him, meaning divine strengthening and support
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this affair, referring to the divinely appointed holder of the matter
key_terms.لَيَغِيبَنَّ: will surely go into absence or occultation
key_terms.مِيثَاقَهُ: His covenant, meaning Allah’s binding pledge with the believer

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the confusion during the ghaybah and who will remain saved?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the ghaybah of the Sahib al-Amr and the intense confusion that will affect people during that period, including the appearance of multiple ambiguous banners. It teaches that salvation in that trial belongs to those firmly grounded by Allah through covenant, iman, and divine support. It also affirms that the truth of the Ahl al-Bayt's matter remains intrinsically clear, even amid outward confusion.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Muawiya, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Ibrahim Bin Khalaf Bin Abbad Al Anmaty, from Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, and with himasws were some people in the room. So I thought that heasws intended by that, others than me (when) heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! Heasws would be absent from you all, the Masterasws of this command, and this (matter) would become so obscure to the extent that it would be said, ‘Heasws died, perished in whichever valley heasws travelled’, and you all would be tossed about just as the ship gets tossed in the waves of the sea. None will be save except for the one whose Covenant Allahazwj has Taken, and Written the Eman to be in his heart, and Aided him with a Spirit from Himazwj. And there would be raised twelve resembling flags. It would not be known which is from which’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I wept’, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What makes you weep, O Abu Abdullah?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How can I not weep and you<sup>asws</sup> are saying there would be twelve resembling flags, not being know which one is from which?’

And in his<sup>asws</sup> gathering there was a skylight through which the sunshine entered. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It this clear (enough)?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Our<sup>asws</sup> matter would be clearer than this sunshine’.
en.sarwar: 11. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mu‘awiya from ‘Abdallah ibn Jabala from Ibrahim ibn Khalaf ibn ‘Abbad al-Anmati from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following.

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and there other people also were present so I thought the Imam (a.s.) meant people other thanme when he said, “By Allah, the in chrage of this task (Leadership with Divine Authority) will disappear from your sight and this (case) will become so obscure that people will say, “He is dead, destroyed or no one knows in which valley has he traveled. You will be shaken just as the ship is shaken in the rough seas and choppy water. No one will remain safe except those in whose hear He has written faith and has supported with an spirit from Him. You will raise twelve identical flags so much so that one would not know which is whiCh”

The narrator has said, “I then wept.” The Imam (a.s.) asked, “what has caused you to weep, O abu ‘Abdallah ?” I then said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, “How can I stop weeping when you say, “Twelve identical flags. . “

The narrator has said that the place of gathering sun light had come in through a whole. The Imam (a.s.) said, “Is this (sun light on the spot) clear?” I said, “Yes, it is clear.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “ our case is clear even more than this.”
